Triangular correlation matrix with coefficient labels

Source: R/plot_corr_triangle.R
plot_corr_triangle.Rd

Reproduces the classic "correlation triangle" style: a lower-triangular matrix of pairwise assay (protein) correlations drawn as coloured circles with the numeric correlation printed inside each circle. Row labels on the left, column labels on the bottom.

Usage

plot_corr_triangle(
  data,
  method = "spearman",
  assay_col = NULL,
  value_col = NULL,
  sample_col = NULL,
  wide = NULL,
  top_n = 30,
  show_values = NULL,
  circle_size = NULL,
  order = "hclust",
  title = NULL,
  palette = NULL,
  x_angle = NULL,
  ...
)

Arguments

data

A data.frame in long format (or wide if `wide = TRUE`), or an OlinkExperiment.

method

Correlation method: "pearson", "spearman" (default), or "kendall".

assay_col

Name of the assay column (long format). If NULL, auto-detected.

value_col

Name of the NPX value column (long format). If NULL, auto-detected.

sample_col

Name of the sample ID column (long format). If NULL, auto-detected.

wide

If TRUE, data is in wide format with samples as rows. If NULL (default), format is detected automatically.

top_n

Limit to the top N assays by variance (default 30).

show_values

Logical; if TRUE, print the numeric correlation coefficient inside each circle. If NULL (default), values are shown, except in journal-size mode (`options(olinkviz.base_size)` below 11) when the circles are too small to hold them at the tick-label size (under about 6.4 mm at 7 pt).

circle_size

Diameter of the circles (ggplot mm). If NULL (default), 14 mm; in journal-size mode (`options(olinkviz.base_size)` below 11) the circles instead fill their grid cell in a single 89 mm column: 85 percent of 65 mm divided by the number of assays, at most 14 mm. Set it explicitly for a wider figure.

order

Ordering of rows/columns: "hclust" (default), "AOE", "FPC", "alphabet", or "original".

title

Plot title.

palette

Optional themed palette for the circle fills: a palette name from `olinkviz_palettes()` (e.g. `"jewel"`) or a character vector of 5 hex colors. Correlations are mapped onto 5 diverging bins (strong negative ... strong positive). If NULL (default), the classic rose/green/orange scheme is used (rose for negative, green/orange for positive).

x_angle

Angle of the column labels in degrees. If NULL (default), 60; 90 (vertical, which never overlaps its neighbours) in journal-size mode (`options(olinkviz.base_size)` below 11).

...

Additional arguments passed to `ggplot2::theme()`.

Value

A ggplot object.

Details

Circles are filled rose/pink for negative correlations, green (weak) or orange (strong) for positive correlations; the circle border encodes significance tiers (blue / orange / red), and strong correlations get a thick border - the same green/orange + border style as the reference correlation-triangle plot, with negatives in rose/pink.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
plot_corr_triangle(beatmg_npx, top_n = 20)
} # }
